title: Activation annealing playbook for heterogeneous A/B slices (WIP)
content:
Status: working draft. Purpose: capture a pragmatic, cross-functional procedure for progressive exposure of heterogeneous experiment slices using a traffic-annealing approach. Designed for LLM features (generation, rerankers, rerouting) where slices differ by model, region, or customer tier and where latency/cost SLOs and behavioral safety both matter.

Context and motivation:
- We keep having oscillation / flip-flop between aggressive canaries (fast exposure) and overly conservative holds (slow learn). For multi-slice experiments, that oscillation multiplies risk: noisy signals from small slices cause premature rollbacks or unnecessary roll-forwards.
- This playbook introduces the "traffic annealing" concept (exposure temperature scheduling + cooldown windows + orthogonal signals) to reduce false positives and provide consistent stakeholder expectations.

Key concepts (quick glossary):
- Annealing (exposure schedule): a controlled, time-boxed ramp of traffic from 0% -> target % driven by an exposure temperature and an attenuation factor.
- Exposure temperature: numeric value (0.0-1.0) representing how aggressively traffic is increased. 1.0 = full planned ramp cadence, 0.0 = frozen/fallback.
- Attenuation factor (alpha): per-slice multiplier applied to the base ramp to reflect fragility (alpha in 0.1-1.0).
- Cooldown window: mandatory observation period after each ramp step during which automated escalations are suppressed unless critical safety signals trigger.
- Orthogonal signals: primary product/quality metrics + infra (latency, OOMs) + cost + abuse/safety heuristics used together to gate exposure.

Scope and when to use this playbook:
- Multi-slice canaries (>=3 concurrently different slices) or A/B experiments that vary serving model, quantization profile, or region routing.
- Not necessary for trivial single-slice experiments where traffic is homogeneous and historical confidence exists.

Roles & responsibilities (minimal cross-functional matrix):
- Experiment owner (PO/PM): hypothesis, slice definitions, target exposure, critical primary metrics, stakeholders contact list.
- Experiment engineer (Eng): traffic routing config, synthetic traffic harness, metric dashboards, emergency kill switch.
- Observability lead (SRE/Obs): telemetry mapping, alert thresholds, dashboard ownership, synthetic workload definition.
- Safety reviewer (Safety/Trust): quick sanity checks on sample outputs, escalations for harmful outputs.
- Customer/comms owner (GTM/CS): external messaging plan if customer-facing.

Annealing schedule (recommended default):
- Preflight (T-48h): smoke tests in staging, synthetic telemetry run, runbook and oncall roster confirmed.
- Step 0 (T0): 0.5% global traffic to each slice for 30 minutes, exposure_temperature=0.2, cooldown=30m.
- Step 1 (T0+1h): 2% -> 5% depending on slice fragility (alpha applied), cooldown=1h.
- Step 2 (T0+4h): 10% (if no triggers), cooldown=2h.
- Step 3 (T0+24h): target steady-state (e.g., 20% or per-hypothesis target).
Notes: these numbers are defaults — adjust by workload. For high-risk slices (safety concerns, fragile models) set alpha <= 0.3 and require extended cooldowns. For low-risk slices (hotfixes, perf-only) alpha can be 0.7-1.0.

Signal definitions and gating rules (must combine signals, not single-source decisions):
- Primary product signals (per-slice, percentile): user success metric (P95 query satisfaction or proxy like click-through or rerank acceptance), degrade >5% relative to control sustained over cooldown -> halt.
- Latency signals: P95 endpoint latency increase >20% absolute or error rate spike >0.5% sustained (configurable) -> step back 1 annealing level.
- Resource signals: GPU OOM, container restarts >3/min -> immediate freeze + rollback to last known-good variant.
- Safety/abuse heuristics: content policy triggers per 1k requests > threshold (e.g., 2x baseline) -> immediate hold + urgent safety review.
- Cost signals: token cost/unit > budgeted threshold for X hours -> notify and consider partial exposure to cheaper model variants.

Decision logic (state machine, simplified):
- At each annealing step end, evaluate windowed signals across last N minutes (N = cooldown duration).
- If any critical signal (OOM, safety breach, infra failure) -> immediate rollback and incident comms.
- If combination of non-critical but consistent degradations (two out of: product metric, latency, or cost) for entire cooldown -> step back one level and increase alpha attenuation by 0.1 for the remainder of the experiment.
- If signals are stable or trending positive -> continue to next step per schedule.

Statistical and sampling guidance for heterogenous slices:
- Per-slice sample sizing: ensure minimum N requests per slice per step for primary metrics. For consumer-facing rerankers, target >= 2,000 meaningful interactions per slice per step to avoid churny variance.
- Interleaved assignment: prefer deterministic hashing by user_id or region to avoid cross-contamination; use sticky routing for at least 48h to capture user-level behavior.
- Control set: always maintain a matched control group routed to current production model variant (not zero-exposure) to serve as baseline.

Synthetic traffic and chaos harnesses (preflight and annealing windows):
- Preflight must run: 30m high-QPS synthetic run with canonical prompts, worst-case long-sequence prompts, and payloads targeting known edge-cases.
- During annealing, run low-rate synthetic probes (1-2 RPS) to detect regressions faster than organic traffic. These feeds should exercise safety heuristics and latency extremes.

Practical knobs and safety abstractions (engineer checklist):
- exposure_temperature variable in runtime config (mutable) to pause or accelerate ramps without reconfiguring routes.
- per-slice alpha stored in experiment metadata for dynamic attenuation.
- automatic cooldown enforcement: no automated step increases while a cooldown active unless explicitly overridden by experiment owner (needs approval and audit log).
- synthetic-probe channel and emergency-kill API endpoints documented in runbook.

Comms and stakeholder cadence during annealing:
- Hourly snapshot during first 6 hours with: per-slice P50/P95 latency, primary metric delta vs control, safety hits, infra incidents, cost burn rate.
- Daily summary after stable at target for first 72h.
- If rollback occurs, owner circulates incident note within 2 hours and schedules a post-mortem within 3 business days.

Recovery and roll-forward patterns:
- Rollback to last known-good variant if critical.
- If step-back occurs due to noisy signals, implement one mitigation (e.g., tighten prompt sanitizer, reduce sequence length, switch quantization) before reattempt. Increase cooldown by 50% on reattempt.

Quick runbook checklist (preflight -> post):
- [ ] Owner defined, stakeholders paged, oncall roster set.
- [ ] Synthetic preflight run completed, artifacts linked.
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts built and sanity-checked.
- [ ] Exposure temperature and per-slice alpha set.
- [ ] Emergency-kill tested.
- [ ] Communication templates prepared (internal + customer-facing).
- [ ] Post-mortem template ready.

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve in design reviews:
- How to normalize primary metric across slices with different customer segments and intents? (suggestion: use propensity-weighted metrics where possible).
- Should exposure schedules be auto-tuned by ML on historical noise metrics? (pro: efficiency; con: opaque decisioning for PG/CS).
- Best practice for cost-budget gating tied to billing alerts (tight coupling may cause false halts during transient token spikes).

Appendix: example annealing config snippet (pseudo):
- experiment: new-reranker-v3
- slices: [region-us, region-eu, enterprise-beta]
- exposures: base_ramp: [0.5%, 2%, 10%, 20%]
- alphas: [0.7, 0.5, 0.2]
- cooldowns: [30m, 1h, 2h, 24h]
- exposure_temperature: 0.5 (start)

Next steps (for this doc):
- Validate default numbers with two live pilot experiments (priority: reranker and generation inference path).
- Build a small dashboard template and a canned synthetic probe set.
- Run a tabletop exercise with oncall and safety reviewers.

Notes to self: keep examples concrete and incorporate feedback from Michael (obs edge cases) and Priya (safety thresholds). This is intentionally prescriptive (defaults) to reduce ambiguity during ops.

End of draft.
